reason: The lug coil's constant-force strip is not in the claim model, and its only realisation that keeps the number runs inside the cuff liner. The drum rides on the carriage's posterior-proximal lug, entirely proximal of the shell, so the strip has no shell under it and must run to an arm-fixed anchor. The independent verifier's X3 check (running at audit time) prices two realisations on the claim bench: the free chord keeps 14.06 (0 new contacts, 0 new lost; 1 pose with the strip < 2 mm from the skin), but the chord's lowest point is at radius 76.61 mm against the liner surface R_liner 79.1 mm, i.e. 2.49 mm into the 4 mm liner on some pose; a 1 mm guide arc under the strip clashes with the chain (< 1 mm) on 326 of 417 evaluated poses (gap 172.4). The number therefore stands only if an unguided spring strip may run through 2.5 mm of liner, which neither the model nor the row states.

reason: The relay's return spring is unmeasured on this hardware, and this row lengthens its travel. R17 is inherited from proxtrack (0.063 N.m preload, coil >= 0.79 N, gravity at phi 0, which depends on the axis only). The row's own arithmetic leaves the 2.0 N constant-force coil 0.22-0.62 N over gravity plus tape friction (0.78 N + mu 0.15-0.25 x 4 N = 1.38-1.78 N), an 11-31 % margin, with the coil moved to a new lug (12 x 10) and the carriage now travelling to phi 39.88. Carriage return, hysteresis, the 3 bistable relay poses and the cuff twist when the carriage lags are not on file. Upheld on the parent by its skeptic; nothing here measures it.
